situation: Inherited a signup funnel handling ~100K applications/year with a ~50% completion rate.
task: Own the frontend end to end, identify drop-off causes, and measurably improve completion.
action: Instrumented the funnel with structured telemetry, identified the biggest friction points, rebuilt key form steps with better validation UX, and added performance checks to CI.
result: Completion grew from ~50% to ~75% across hundreds of thousands of applications.
reflection: Set up telemetry on day one rather than reverse-engineering drop-off from logs.

situation: A growing frontend codebase had increasing cross-feature coupling; reviews were slow and ownership unclear.
task: Lead a framework migration that also established long-term architectural direction.
action: Proposed and executed a vertical-slice architecture, codified dependency direction with lint rules, and documented conventions.
result: Smaller reviewable PRs, explicit ownership, faster onboarding.
reflection: Involve the team earlier in the design phase to surface edge cases and build buy-in sooner.
